verdicts.correctedClaim: Engine North Node minus Swiss TRUE_NODE (TT pinned, 2025) carries a -7.3" mean bias (p50 7.0", max 16.7" on every-3rd-day sampling; 19.9" on the auditor's daily grid), and it is not a definition difference: rebuilding the node from Swiss's own of-date geometric Moon state reproduces TRUE_NODE to p50 0.95", max 2.92", mean -0.07". The cause is the analytic (Improved Lunar Ephemeris) Moon STATE error in both components, not the velocity alone: in a common J2000 frame, node(AE r, AE v) - node(Swiss r, Swiss v) has mean -7.27"; node(AE r, Swiss v) has mean -3.63" and node(Swiss r, AE v) has mean -3.64" (AE-Swiss velocity difference p50 0.03 m/s). Since GeoMoonState differences the same series, both halves come from the series and the fix (DE-based Moon state) is unchanged. The committed 6.07" six-case maximum (README:64) understates it.

Attribution by component swapping between A.GeoMoonState (EQJ) and Swiss FLG_J2000 geometric state, node taken on the J2000 ecliptic: AE-state node minus Swiss-state node mean -7.269" (p50 7.09, max 16.87, i.e. the full bias survives the frame change); AE position + Swiss velocity: mean -3.63" (p50 3.38, max 11.15); Swiss position + AE velocity: mean -3.64" (p50 2.70, max 16.25); the two halves sum to the total (cross term negligible). So 'provably a Moon-velocity error' is half the story; position error of the same series contributes equally. Code path (chunk-GBH7JIYF.js:50-63, astronomy.js:2884-2897 dt=1e-5 d central difference) confirmed as described. Severity stays major: the node is the largest residual of the twelve points and Swiss's own method is ~1-3" internally.

notes: Method: independent scripts under <audit>/verify/production-positions/ (engine-verify.mjs -> engine-verify.json; de440-verify.py via the auditor's jplvenv -> de440-verify.json; swiss-verify.py in <swisslab>/venv -> swiss-verify.json; modern-deltat.mjs/.json). Sampling deliberately differs from the auditor (every 3rd day of 2025, 122 instants; 8 epochs; 54 ASC cases incl. Helsinki and Sydney); p50/mean statistics agree with the auditor to ~0.05\" and maxima are slightly lower only where the coarser grid misses a peak (Moon 3.63 vs 2.99\", node 19.9 vs 16.7\"). Every Swiss call asserted retflag has FLG_SWIEPH and not FLG_MOSEPH; the .se1 files answered every instant 1800-02-01..2399-12-01. No new Horizons requests were made: the auditor's seven cached responses were re-parsed from the raw text (all show source DE441, TT, GEOCENTRIC) and compared afresh; Horizons Q31 is documented in the response as IAU76/80 ecliptic-of-date, which accounts for the constant +0.046\" Swiss offset and is irrelevant at the engine's 8-15\" residuals. The worktree was only read. One substantive correction: finding 4's cause is the analytic Moon state error in both position and velocity (about -3.6\" each), not the velocity alone; conclusions and fix unchanged. Finding 3 is understated for 60N cities (Helsinki 36\" shipped ASC error, reduced to 0.12\" with the true obliquity), consistent with the auditor's own 39.9\" analytic bound. Severity 'major' is appropriate for all six under the stated rules; none contradicts an explicit documented guarantee (the README hedges its six-case maxima and already concedes the 2100 Delta-T gap), so none rises to blocking.
